chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya al-Tawil al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who is commanded to do good and forbidden from evil is a believer who takes heed, or an ignorant person who learns; but as for the owner of the whip and sword, he will not (listen).

key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: the good (what is recognized as virtuous)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ سَوْطٍ وَسَيْفٍ: the owner of the whip and sword (ruler/authority relying on force)
key_terms.عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ: from the evil (what is recognized as wrong)

ai.seo_question: Who is the effective recipient of enjoining good and forbidding evil according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the intellectual efficacy of *Amr bil Ma'ruf* and the coercive nature of authority (*Sultan*). He clarifies that the command is primarily a means of admonition for the receptive believer or education for the ignorant, whereas for the ruler or authority figure relying on the 'whip and sword,' it serves a different, often punitive or administrative, function rather than spiritual guidance. This reflects the Shia scholarly distinction between the scholarly duty of enjoining good and the political reality of governance.
